**Test image analysis:**
- Tomato leaf with large, irregular, tan/brown papery necrotic patches covering ~35% of the leaf
- Lesions are dry and appear to have a slightly fuzzy/rough texture
- Amorphous shape, not target-spot rings or small circular lesions
- Green leaf tissue remaining appears healthy

**Reasoning:**
The large irregular tan-brown papery lesions with a slightly fuzzy surface texture are characteristic of Gray Mold (Botrytis cinerea). This doesn't match Early Blight (concentric ring target spots), Septoria (small circular spots with dark margins), Late Blight (dark water-soaked lesions), or Bacterial Speck (tiny dark specks). The reference Gray Mold image confirmed the grayish-brown necrotic appearance, though it showed fruit — Botrytis on leaves produces the same tan papery necrosis seen here.
